# Lumiose UI

> `@lumiose/ui`: accessible, unstyled UI primitives built on native elements (`<dialog>`, popover, invoker commands, CSS anchor positioning), server-rendered without hydration. Style them with your own CSS or the optional default theme.

These docs ship in `@lumiose/ui` and match the installed version: `node_modules/@lumiose/ui/docs`.
In a project that depends on it, `lumiose docs ui` prints the index and `lumiose docs dialog` a
component's page; the Lumiose MCP server's `ui_components` tool lists every component's parts,
props, events and styling hooks. The Lumiose docs: `node_modules/lumiose/docs/llms.txt`.

## Overview

- [UI components](README.md): `@lumiose/ui`: accessible, unstyled UI primitives built on native elements (`<dialog>`, popover, invoker commands, CSS anchor positioning), server-rendered without hydration. Style them with your own CSS or the optional default theme.
- [Installation](installation.md): Add `@lumiose/ui` to a Lumiose app and import its stylesheets, and the default theme if you want its look. The components then render in server HTML, without an island, and a page loads only the small scripts of the components it renders.
- [Theming](theming.md): `@lumiose/ui` is unstyled: its stylesheets hold only what the components need to work. The optional default theme gives them a look, light and dark, through `--lu-` custom properties you can change; or style the parts with your own CSS.

## Components

- [Accordion](accordion.md): A stack of items whose triggers show and hide their panels, after the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern: each item is a native `<details>`, one open at a time through the browser's exclusive group (`name`) or several, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript and find-in-page opens the item it lands in. `<lu-accordion>`, a 1 kB light-DOM element, adds the arrow keys and Base UI's animation hooks. `bind:value` (or `value` and `onValueChange`) keeps a signal in sync.
- [Checkbox](checkbox.md): A native `<input type="checkbox">`, after Base UI's Checkbox: Space and a label click toggle it, the form submits its value when checked, reset and `required` work, in server HTML and without JavaScript. `indeterminate`, `readOnly`, the parent checkbox of a Checkbox Group and `bind:checked` come on top, with a 0.5 kB script shared with Radio Group and Switch.
- [Checkbox Group](checkbox-group.md): A group of checkboxes with one value, the list of the checked ones, after Base UI's CheckboxGroup: a native `<fieldset>` whose checkboxes share a name, so the form submits each checked value and a disabled group disables them all, without JavaScript. A parent checkbox checks them all and shows checked, mixed or unchecked as they are; `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.
- [Collapsible](collapsible.md): A panel that its trigger shows and hides: a native `<details>` whose `<summary>` is the trigger, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, keeps the browser's keyboard handling, and opens when find-in-page or a link lands inside it. A 0.7 kB script adds Base UI's animation hooks. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.
- [Combobox](combobox.md): A text input that filters a list of options, for picking one value or several from many: the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with list autocomplete, after Base UI's Combobox. The input shows the option's label and the form gets its value. `<lu-combobox>`, a 3.8 kB form-associated light-DOM element, runs it on server-rendered pages and in islands; `bind:value` and `bind:open` keep signals in sync. Groups, an empty state, a status, a clear button, multiple values with chips, validation and async options.
- [Dialog](dialog.md): A modal dialog, or an alert dialog that needs an answer: a native `<dialog>` opened and closed by invoker commands, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, and a 0.8 kB script closes the native element's gaps where JavaScript runs. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.
- [Field](field.md): A form field: a label, a native control, a description and its errors, wired with `for`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`, after Base UI's Field. Validation is the browser's constraint validation (`required`, `type`, `pattern`, `minlength`…); a 1.0 kB script shows it in the field's Error parts at the right time, instead of the browser's bubble, and focuses the first invalid field on submit. A Form's server errors render in the HTML, so they work without JavaScript.
- [Fieldset](fieldset.md): A group of related fields with a caption: a native `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`, after Base UI's Fieldset. The browser names the group by its legend and disables every control inside a disabled fieldset, with no JavaScript and no CSS of its own. The legend also names a Checkbox Group or a Radio Group.
- [Form](form.md): A native `<form>` that hands its fields the server's errors, after Base UI's Form. Pass the data a form action gives `fail()` as `errors`, and each Field shows the message for its `name`, in the HTML the server renders back (no JavaScript needed) or, with `submit()`, in an island. Submission, validation and the first invalid field's focus are the platform's and Field's.
- [Input](input.md): A native `<input>`, after Base UI's Input: every type, constraint and autofill the browser has, plus `onValueChange` and `bind:value`. Inside a Field (as `Field.Control`) it takes the field's id, name and ARIA references. No script, no CSS of its own.
- [Menu](menu.md): A menu of commands, links, checkbox and radio items and submenus, opened by a button: the trigger's `popovertarget` opens it and CSS anchor positioning places it, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, and a 3.3 kB script adds the APG Menu Button keyboard contract where JavaScript runs. `bind:open`, `bind:checked` and `bind:value` keep signals in sync in islands.
- [Popover](popover.md): A popup anchored to its trigger: a native `popover` opened and closed by the trigger's `popovertarget`, placed with CSS anchor positioning, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript. A 1.7 kB script moves focus into it and back, dismisses it as Base UI does (not on a right-click), keeps `aria-expanded` current and places it in browsers without anchor positioning. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.
- [Radio](radio-group.md): A group of radios with one value, after Base UI's RadioGroup and Radio: native radios in a `<fieldset role="radiogroup">`. The browser gives the group one tab stop, arrow keys that move and select (skipping disabled radios), `required`, submission and reset, in server HTML and without JavaScript; a legend names the group. `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.
- [Select](select.md): A native `<select>` for picking one value from a list: it works with no JavaScript, submits with its form and keeps the platform's keyboard, typeahead and mobile pickers. Where the browser has customizable select (`appearance: base-select`, Chrome 135, Safari 27), `Select.Trigger` and `Select.Value` shape the button, the picker is styleable and options may hold more than text; elsewhere it is the classic select. No script; `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync in islands.
- [Switch](switch.md): On or off, for a setting: a native `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">`, after Base UI's Switch. Space and a label click toggle it, the form submits its value when on, `required` and reset work, in server HTML and without JavaScript, and assistive technology announces a switch. `bind:checked` keeps a signal in sync.
- [Tabs](tabs.md): A tab list and the panel of the selected tab, after the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: the server HTML holds the whole state (roles, `aria-selected`, the roving tab stop, the hidden panels), and `<lu-tabs>`, a 0.8 kB light-DOM element, adds the arrow keys and the selection. Manual or automatic activation, horizontal or vertical, right-to-left aware; `bind:value` (or `value` and `onValueChange`) keeps a signal in sync.
- [Toast](toast.md): Short notices in a region of their own, after Base UI's toast: server HTML renders them (a form action's result), and islands add, update and close them through a toast manager. `<lu-toast-viewport>`, a 2.3 kB light-DOM element, puts them in the top layer, times them (pausing on hover and focus), limits how many show, closes them on a swipe, Escape or their close button, focuses the region on F6, and makes screen readers announce them.
- [Tooltip](tooltip.md): A short tip next to its trigger, on hover or keyboard focus: a native `popover="hint"` with `role="tooltip"`, placed with CSS anchor positioning. The trigger is described by the tip in server HTML, so screen readers announce it without hovering; a 1.5 kB script opens and closes it as Base UI's tooltip does. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.
